title: County of Artois
capsule: The County of Artois was created in 1237 when Louis IX of France granted it as an apanage to his brother Robert I, defining a distinct feudal unit out of the old county of Arras whose capital was at Arras. It passed through the Capetian apanage line until Robert II's death at the Battle of Courtrai in 1302, after which it was contested between France and the Flemish-linked house of Mahaut. The attestation window 1241–1333 covers the period of clearest independent comital rule before Artois was absorbed into the Duchy of Burgundy in 1384 and subsequently into Habsburg and then French royal domains. The region gave its name to the artesian well, reflecting the geology of the chalk basin.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The county's existence and political history are well documented in French medieval records; territorial extent is clearly defined by the feudal grant and corresponds closely to the modern Pas-de-Calais département.
